why: Design 1 with R split, so rest is truly quiet and detection stays sensitive. R1 is a near-critical detector on 8 (F - SL) (self 4.4, bias -2.26: on above ~0.10, off below ~0.02), with no output to the wall, so its leaky resting state cannot drive the wall or the comparator. R2 is a clean driver (self 4, bias -6, driven 8 by R1): off at rest (~0.01), on (~0.98) while R1 is on. It runs the front half (-2 + 8 cos theta) and sends the efference copy (-7.2 to F and SL). Runs start when the light's elevation above its slow level crosses ~0.1 (sensor noise in dim light fires exploring runs), continue while the light keeps rising, and stop when the elevation falls to ~0.02. Darkness is still.
